home.hero.title: I'm not a developer. I built a 14-agent system that runs my sales job anyway.
home.hero.sub: I'm Jai, Applied AI Lead at Turing College, a YC-backed edtech. History degree, sales career, no formal technical training. Three months with Claude Code changed what I could build. My job now is helping enterprises give their people the same jump, and I write about it weekly.
home.gtm-card.body: Enterprise sales for AI apprenticeships in the UK: 6 to 10 discovery calls a week, self-built qualification frameworks, an outbound engine audited across 100+ campaigns. I treat pipeline as an engineering problem and publish the frameworks that survive contact with real deals.
home.ai-card.body: Multi-week Claude Code curricula, monthly live workshops, demos where the audience ships something before they leave. In the last series every participant deployed a live website in-session. I build the attendee hubs, run sheets and sandboxes myself.
home.bridge.title: Why one site for both
home.bridge.body: I sell AI capability by day and run that sales job on agents I built at night. I took this role because I believe the average person can become properly AI capable and future proof themselves, whatever happens to their job title. I'm the test case. Everything here is either the selling, the building, or the teaching of that one idea.
home.subscribe.title: AI with Jai, weekly
home.subscribe.body: One idea a week on closing the gap between knowing AI and using it. Written for operators, L&D teams and anyone whose job title is about to change.
gtm.hero.sub: I sell employer-funded AI apprenticeships to UK enterprises. A typical week is 6 to 10 discovery calls, 3 or 4 concurrent enterprise cycles, and a mock presentation before any pitch that matters. The rest of this page is how the engine behind that works.
ai.hero.sub: My rule for every session: the audience ships something before they leave. Slides are for context. The point is a working artefact, made by the attendee, live by the end.
writing.hero.sub: I publish weekly at AI with Jai. The running thread is the knowing-doing gap: why giving people AI tools changes so little, and what actually makes a person or a team capable. This page updates itself from the Substack feed.
